A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: Experiments 1–3 report original regression analyses of reading times, GPT2 probability manipulations, and similarity-adjusted surprisal using existing human datasets.

after.justification: Retains the original empirical analyses and adds clustering-stability results, qualitative cluster examples, and individual-run results in Appendices B–C.

M1.justification: The GPT2 model, cloze smoothing, three probability manipulations, and similarity-adjusted surprisal procedure are retained. Renaming the smoothing factor from S to V and discussing an unimplemented alternative to H2 do not change the method.

E1.justification: Both versions use BK21 SPR, Provo eye-tracking, and UCL SPR/eye-tracking data with the same six reading-time measures. The added diagnostics examine existing clustering and sampling outputs without expanding dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same baseline regression predictors and comparisons involving cloze, GPT2, manipulated GPT2, combined predictors, SA-Cloze, and SA-GPT2. Newly cited approaches are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Appendix B introduces a supplementary evaluation protocol: pairwise Adjusted Rand Index comparisons among five clustering runs for each k. Existing reading-time filtering, folds, observation counts, model configurations, and regression evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds targeted checks of cluster stability and semantic coherence through Figure 6 and Table 3, plus individual-run robustness displays for H1 and H2 in Figures 9–10. These supplement the retained smoothing, cluster-count, and frequency-threshold analyses.

E5.justification: V2 expands variability reporting through clustering-agreement boxplots and individual-run results previously summarized by medians. Both versions already specify five sampling/clustering runs; there is no reported increase. Existing fold-based SEMs, permutation tests, and Bonferroni corrections are retained.

E6.justification: Existing main results, table values, and appendix sensitivity results are unchanged. V2 adds clustering agreement that decreases with k while remaining above chance, cluster examples, individual-run outcomes, and token-splitting rates of 5.1%, 5.9%, and 1.9% for BK21, Provo, and UCL.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5 retain their mathematical content; S-to-V renaming is equivalent notation. The added Adjusted Rand Index analysis uses an existing empirical metric without introducing a new formal definition, derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The conclusion now qualifies the LM predictive advantage as applying 'at least for eyetracking data,' narrowing the earlier general statement about reading times. The central contribution and claimed support for all three hypotheses remain intact.

C2.justification: V2 suggests task differences rather than data noise as an explanation for weak SPR fits. It adds qualifications about overlapping hypotheses, H2 simplification, and inconclusive superlinearity, and expands discussion of structural processing and explicit links between cognitive processes and measured behavior.

D1.justification: New figure captions clarify that median log likelihood is calculated separately within each fold. Appendix B identifies static token embeddings and specifies the cluster examples' configuration, run, and corpus. These are reporting refinements; existing hyperparameters and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds contextual literature on structure building, predictive coding, task differences, nonlinear surprisal effects, and clustering validation while retaining its central research positioning. Giulianelli et al.'s preprint-to-publication update refers to the same work and is not a new citation.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized revisions to the introduction, interpretations, conclusion, and explanatory footnotes, adds acknowledgments, and reorganizes appendix material. The main section sequence and three-experiment narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: The appendix presentation is substantially expanded with clustering boxplots, a cluster-example table, and two sets of individual-run panels. Existing sensitivity figures are enlarged and reformatted onto separate pages. The smoothing table moves into the main text; main Figures 1–5 remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added cluster validation and individual-run displays make previously aggregated evidence more inspectable. The eye-tracking qualification and expanded interpretive caveats better align conclusions with the evidence. These are useful but bounded improvements; the methods, coverage, and main empirical findings remain unchanged.
